shared-edit apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/runtime_registries.rs: McpRegistry::replace_org is a merge (upsert the answer, then remove only keys absent from it) and returns the removed ids. A discovery-catalog entry is kept while the server's url, transport, allowlist, enabled flag and token are unchanged, and dropped when it changed or the server is new or gone. hydrate_mcp_registry swaps the ownership sidecar the same way (upsert first, remove after the row is gone), through apply_mcp_projection, so a server in both the old and the new answer is never missing at any instant. The ownership sidecar has no way to list its keys, so only the ownership of rows the registry dropped is removed; an ownership record with no registry row behind it is not cleaned by a successful refresh (it is by a clear).

WS04-S4: shared-edit apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md: WS04 S4 review rulings (all implemented, flag off by default). (0) A failed read of the thread grant (timeout past 5 s, Unavailable, Unimplemented from an older session-core, a refusal) is NOT 'no grant': with MODEL_GATEWAY_DURABLE_PLAN_GRANT on, a non-execute run states READ_ONLY (the narrowest rung; Unspecified would mean unconstrained to execution-core) and an execute run is refused plan_grant_unavailable. Only an Ok answer that says none is no grant. One warn per failure with the status code only, counted in plan_grant_read_failed_total. (1) plan_approval with the flag on retries SetRunMode (first attempt, then retries after about 100, 300 and 900 ms, transient codes only); on final failure the plan stays APPROVED, the answer is persisted:false, and the approving replica records the grant in its in-memory PlanModeStore and keeps honouring it: the run start uses it only when Session Core answers 'no grant', Session Core's own grant always wins, and an unreadable read never consults memory. (2) session-core checks ONCE at boot (information_schema) that the five 0050 grant columns exist. With them absent a stated grant is skipped with a warn (the run UPDATE proceeds) and GetThreadGrant answers 'no grant' without naming the columns. Revert order: gateway flag off, drop the columns, RESTART session-core. (3) The durable exit uses was_active = durable run mode OR this replica's flag (mark_run_plan_mode's durable write is best-effort), and the raw gRPC ExitPlanMode goes through handle_exit_plan_mode_durable when the flag is on. (4) SetRunMode refuses a waived credential that states a grant (durable_mutation_forbidden, FailedPrecondition), as record_run_context does; a waived credential's mode change that states no grant is unchanged.

shared-edit apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md: WS04 S4 second-review rulings (flag off by default). (0) Every in-memory plan-grant fallback is keyed on the run's OWN thread (GetRun's thread_id), never on a caller-supplied session_id. With the durable-grant flag on, gRPC ExitPlanMode refuses a session_id that differs from the run's thread (PermissionDenied) before anything is published or recorded, and answers Unavailable if the run row cannot be read while a session_id is named. The fallback is kept in memory ONLY after a transient SetRunMode failure (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Aborted, ResourceExhausted, Internal), in plan_approval and in gRPC ExitPlanMode; a refusal (FailedPrecondition, PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated, InvalidArgument, NotFound) records no copy. (1) plan_approval sends a waived credential's SetRunMode with the mode change alone (no granted_rung, justification or approved_plan_id), so the run leaves plan mode as before durable grants. The answer is persisted:false, with the flag on the approving replica keeps the grant in memory on the run's own thread, and session-core keeps refusing a waived caller that states a grant as defence in depth. Consequence: a waived approval no longer writes the runs.metadata autonomy_rung/justification copy. The waiver is read through zdr_posture::claims_view.
